status: aspirational — not applied anywhere; no engine-side mechanism exists to apply it against yet
description: The desired grid access-control policy, in fleetsmith's own vocabulary — NOT a RelataDB-native policy format. RelataDB's conditional/cell-level ACL enforcement is not yet wired into every call site on the upstream engine (tracked as RelataDB #3118/#3125/#3126; see docs/architecture/intelligence-grid.md and docs/milestones/v0.7.0-intelligence-grid.md, which already call this out as a known gap, not an assumption made here). This file exists so the desired policy is reviewable now and ready to apply the moment a real engine-side mechanism ships. The OPERATIVE enforcement today is client-side only: ee/src/grid/identity.js's assertPushIdentity(), which refuses to push when a token's principal is discoverable and mismatches the local actor.

rules.rule: a write to any row of these types must be rejected unless the row's actor field (imported_by, for OrgDocument) equals the authenticated token's principal
rules.enforced_by: client-side only (ee/src/grid/identity.js's assertPushIdentity) — no server-side equivalent exists on this engine yet; see the 'status' field above

rules.rule: an OrgDocument row's transition to the 'approved' approval state must be rejected unless the actor carries an approver role
rules.enforced_by: client-side only (ee/src/grid/approval.js's assertApprover, G7.3), checked against grid.approvers/GRID_APPROVERS — a fleet-configured allowlist, not an engine role. Still no server-side equivalent: no role/scope concept has been verified on this engine surface at all, so there is nothing for a real ACL policy to enforce here either, same as the rule above.
